ask: At any point does on-screen text or a graphic cover the speaker's eyes, nose or mouth?
fix: look at the frames where cards and captions sit and move them off the face

ask: Is the framing so tight that the speaker's face is cut off (forehead, chin, or part of the face out of frame) for much of the video?
While someone is talking, are their words missing from the screen, so a viewer with the sound off can't follow?
fix: caption what's said (captions), unless the piece is meant to run without

ask: Is any on-screen text hard to read: too faint against what's behind it, overlapping other text, or too small for a phone?
fix: give the text contrast and room: a scrim or shadow, a stronger colour, one line at a time

ask: Does the video stop before its point lands: mid-sentence, mid-step, or without the ending it set up?
fix: end on a finished sentence and the payoff or the ask the opening promised

ask: Is there a stretch of a second or more with nothing worth looking at: black, blank, frozen or washed out?
fix: give those seconds a picture: a clip, b-roll, the product, or cut them

ask: How clearly does the video get one point across to a viewer who has never heard of the brand?
fix: say the one thing the piece is for earlier and plainer; cut what doesn't serve it

ask: In these opening seconds, is a person's face or the thing being sold clearly on screen?
fix: open on the speaker's face or the product, not a title card or an empty frame

ask: Is there short on-screen text in these opening seconds that gives the viewer a reason to keep watching?
fix: put the hook line on screen in the first second, short and readable

ask: How likely is someone scrolling a feed to stop on this opening?
fix: lead with the most surprising line or picture the takes have; cut the warm-up

ask: The panels are a storyboard in time order, with text drawn as solid bars. In any panel, does a bar or graphic sit over a person's eyes, nose or mouth?
fix: move that text or graphic off the face before rendering

ask: The panels are a storyboard in time order, with text drawn as solid bars. In any panel, do two blocks of text overlap or touch each other?
label_words: stacked on the exact same line
fix: give each line its own band, or show them one after another

ask: The panels are a storyboard in time order. Do most panels look nearly the same, as if the picture barely changes through the video?
fix: vary the picture: punch-ins, b-roll, the product, a designed moment

ask: The panels are a storyboard in time order. Is any panel empty: black, blank, or with nothing to look at?
fix: cover that moment with a clip, b-roll or a card

ask: Is the brand or product name said aloud or shown on screen at some point?
fix: say or show the name: on screen in the first seconds and again at the end

ask: Is the brand's logo or wordmark visible at some point in the video?
fix: place the logo from media/brand on the end card or as a small lockup

ask: How well do the on-screen graphics (type, colours, cards) match the brand described?
fix: take type and colours from brand/brand.css and BRAND.md; drop the house look
